new.analysis:
## What happened last week
**You didn't run last week, and your check-in gives no health reason for it.** You missed all three planned walk-runs, on Mon Sep 21, Wed Sep 23 and Sat Sep 26, and you rested on the rest days. You reported 7.5 hours of sleep, low stress and a body that felt good. If you did run and the watch didn't record it, tell me so I can count it.

## Why the restart is gentle
**Nine days off costs very little fitness, but it's still a reason to step back, not forward.** Early on, your calves and tendons get used to running more slowly than your heart and lungs do, so they decide how fast you can build. That's why most of the week repeats the last level you finished, with one step forward on Saturday.

## The bigger picture
**Missed weeks, not fitness, have kept you at 2-minute run blocks since late August.**

| Week | Walk-runs done | Total time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aug 24 – 30 | 3 of 3 | 64 min |
| Aug 31 – Sep 6 | 3 of 3 | 66 min |
| Sep 7 – 13 | 1 of 3 (cold) | 24 min |
| Sep 14 – 20 | 3 of 3 | 63 min |
| Sep 21 – 27 | 0 of 3 | 0 min |

**Your last run suggests you're ready for longer run blocks.** On Sat Sep 19 it felt like effort 6/10, and your heart rate averaged 135, about 74 percent of your maximum. It also drifted down by about 7 beats as the session went on, which shows your body is coping well with 2-minute blocks.

## The road to Nov 15
**At about 7:40 per km, the 5K is roughly 38 minutes of running without a break.** The plan is to make the run blocks longer most weeks: 3 minutes, then about 5, then 8 to 10, then 15 or more. Before race week you should run 20 to 30 minutes without stopping. That's a realistic path, but it leaves little room for another lost week.

**You won't see any fast sessions, even though this is when faster running usually starts.** For you, the hard part is running for longer, so every session stays easy. Speed work would only make the run blocks harder to keep going.

**Run the blocks slower than feels natural.** If a 3-minute block starts to feel long, slow to a shuffle rather than stopping early to walk. Easing off without stopping is exactly what you'll need on race day.

**If a planned run falls through, move it back a day rather than dropping it.** Push the next run back too if you need to, so you never run two days in a row or squeeze in extra runs. Two runs in a week beats none, and three is the target.
